headline: Healthcare Leads a Broadly Higher Friday; Chips Drag on the Tape
body_html:
Stocks are tilting positive at midday in the final session of the week, with 330 names advancing against 208 declining across the 544-stock universe. Healthcare sits at the top of the sector table, up 1.1%, lifted in part by a near-7% surge in biosimulation specialist Certara and a 5.21% jump in life-science tools maker Repligen. Software is also carrying its weight, adding 0.62%, with cybersecurity name Zscaler pacing that group after climbing more than 5%.

The session's clearest fault line runs through semiconductors, down 0.9%, and homebuilders, the worst-performing sector at minus 1.23%. RF-chip supplier Skyworks Solutions fell 5.21%, audio-chip maker Cirrus Logic shed 4.59%, and power-semiconductor firm ON Semiconductor dropped 3.5%, collectively dragging the chip complex lower. Real-estate brokerage outfit eXp World Holdings leads all decliners, off 5.61%, while Victoria's Secret slipped 5.24% to pressure the consumer-apparel corner.

Into the close, traders will be watching whether the semiconductor weakness broadens or stabilizes — options-market signals around large-cap tech resilience have drawn attention this week. Bond-market jitters flagged in recent commentary add a macro undercurrent. Monday, October 12 will be the first opportunity to respond to any weekend developments.

briefs.headline: Certara Surges to Lead Healthcare Advance
briefs.body: Biosimulation software company Certara jumped nearly 7% Friday, making it the session's top percentage gainer and a primary driver of Healthcare's 1.1% sector-wide gain. Repligen, a life-science tools supplier, added 5.21%, reinforcing the group's outperformance as investors rotated toward defensive growth names late in the week.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Bear the Brunt of Friday's Selling
briefs.body: Semiconductors are the session's weakest major sector, off 0.9%, as Skyworks Solutions, Cirrus Logic, and ON Semiconductor each fell between 3.5% and 5.2%. The losses reflect persistent uncertainty around end-market demand in consumer electronics and power applications, themes that have weighed on the group through much of the autumn.

briefs.headline: Zscaler Anchors a Solid Software Session
briefs.body: Cloud-security provider Zscaler climbed 5.35% midday, anchoring a 0.62% gain for the broader software sector. The move comes as options-market watchers note unusual resilience in large-cap technology names despite macro headwinds, a dynamic analysts say may reflect hedging patterns rather than straightforward directional conviction.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strikes on Riyadh Airport Rattle Regional Aviation
briefs.body: Houthi militants struck Riyadh's airport, killing three Saudi nationals and intensifying the regional conflict, according to Reuters. The European Union's aviation safety authority subsequently widened its airspace warning over Saudi Arabia, a development that drew fresh attention after a major U.S. airline chief said safety considerations would govern any decision to launch Saudi routes.

briefs.headline: Bond-Market Warning Signals Add Macro Overhang
briefs.body: A Reuters analysis flagged four technical and fundamental indicators suggesting conditions in the bond market could deteriorate further. Rising yield volatility has complicated the equity-valuation backdrop heading into the weekend, and traders are watching whether any weekend geopolitical developments amplify that pressure when markets reopen Monday, October 12.

briefs.headline: Prediction Markets Eye Data-Center Buildout Milestone
briefs.body: Traders on forecasting exchange Kalshi are assigning high odds that more than 5,100 data centers will be planned or in operation before 2027, reflecting continued bullish positioning on AI infrastructure demand. Separately, NBA Commissioner Adam Silver disclosed the league wants access to prediction-market data to help detect potential manipulation of game-related contracts.
